question: Can native-selected high-criticality targets receive all-layer search early while other nets retain the existing overuse-triggered layer expansion, recovering quality/success benefits with less broad search?
new_mechanism: After setup/pruning and native remaining-target criticality computation, persistently expand only the layer limits of a net with a remaining target at criticality>=.9. Preserve XY bounds, native costs, route/guide transactions, native reroute selection and existing overuse layer feedback. No guide in first independent test.

arms.C: new mode absent, old feedback0, reproduce original A0
arms.O: new mode absent, existing overuse feedback1, independent adaptive baseline
arms.Z: critical threshold0 plus existing feedback1, must reproduce initial-global A1 complete route/metrics

gates: Default-off exact native A0 including failure status; Z exact A1 including native FULL and route equivalence. All legal routes independently graph-audited, failed CPD excluded. Compare C/O/A1/K with CPD/resources/iterations/planning and process costs; no formal timing or guide-causality claim.
scope: New early criticality trigger differs from already implemented pre-prune overuse witness. Do not present the old witness policy as novel. If useful, verify fixed settings on additional circuits before combining with Tf.
